thread:
alex: ran a profiling pass on rtxp cluster, noticed p99 explosions on long-context requests even though p50/p95 look fine. dumping notes.
alex: quick summary: p50=95ms, p95=120ms, p99=640ms. throughput ~450 tok/s baseline. when microbatch size bumped 8->12 throughput +10% but p99 +2.5x for long seqs.
maria: which kernel path are those requests hitting? any kernel swaps visible?
alex: we see a kernel switch at ~1k tokens. short paths use aten_attn_v2, long paths take fused_flash path. swap causes a serialization pause and high KV-cache churn.
jiho: can you paste the flamegraph / perf output?
alex: pasted snippet:
```
perf record -g -o /tmp/p.record ./serve --model x
perf script | stackcollapse-perf.pl > out.folded
flamegraph.pl out.folded > flame.svg
# hot spots: fused_flash_cu, kv_cache_eviction, memcpy_sync
```
alex: notable: kv_cache_eviction rate jumps 7x when kernel swaps happen -> GC-style pauses, plus memcpy_sync during kernel load.
sam: my 2c: consider a soft sequence_prune policy (early-stop token budget) + hard per-request timeout. soft cap reduces useful work but protects tail.
alex: experimented with soft_max_output_tokens=256 and hard_cap=512. results: p99 down 640->280ms, p95 ~120->110ms. completion drop ~0.8% (clients hit soft cap and stop). throughput stable.
maria: nice. what about batching heuristics? padding is killing us when we mix short+long. maybe bin by context-length and cap microbatch expansion.
jiho: agree. microbatching: keep microbatch target small for >1k contexts, allow larger microbatches for <256 contexts. also add a max_padding_ratio to prevent long requests from being padded too much.
alex: added a short config sketch:
```
serving:
  microbatch_target: 10
  microbatch_max: 20
  max_padding_ratio: 1.4   # reject batches that would pad >40%
  sequence_prune:
    soft_max_tokens: 256
    hard_timeout_ms: 350
  kernel_pinning:
    threshold_tokens: 1024
    prefer_fused: false
```
maria: plus implement fallback routing: if request indicates high tail risk (long context + budget low) route to quantized model or smaller variant. reduces quality but keeps SLOs.
sam: also add KV-cache hysteresis: don't evict unless free_slots < 10% for last 30s, and prefetch popular prefixes. bloom-filter for misses to avoid synchronous loads.
perfbot: perfbot: created experiment 1945678901-seq-prune-canary with 10% traffic, config ref: serving.sequence_prune v1, kernel_pinning enabled, kv_hysteresis v1.
alex: plan: 1) land soft/hard caps + microbatch padding guard 2) enable kernel pin toggle behind flag 3) kv eviction hysteresis + bloom 4) canary 10% with metrics (p50/p95/p99, completion_drop_rate, kv_miss_rate) @maria can you own the rollout and metrics dashboard?
maria: yep. will schedule canary tomorrow 09:30PT, add dashboards and alert if p99 > 300ms or completion_drop_rate > 1% :thumbsup:
jiho: when can we get a post-canary flamegraph? want to validate that memcpy_sync/kernel-load heat drops.
alex: i'll collect profiles during canary and post them here. thanks all.
